what: EST_MINUTES OVERSTATES MEASURED RUNTIME ~8x, AND THE ROUTER AND RUNWAY METRICS USE IT (2026-11-18). MEASURED on the four QUEUE-FILL-W47 units that ran (workflow wall time on the GitHub runner, including ~1 min setup; run ids 44382443666, 44382447562, 44387488936, 44387493913): abab-01 harness_stage0 est 70 min, actual 9.1; abab-02 harness_stage0 est 90, actual 9.6; abab-20 exit_lever_ablation est 30, actual 1.5; abab-38 exit_lever_ablation est 30, actual 7.5. Actual/est = 0.13, 0.11, 0.05, 0.25, median ~0.12 (n = 4, runner only, no Kaggle-kernel timing yet). Separately, ltr_action_trigger_s0.py took 11.2 s against the est of 60 min carried by the ed2b/43b6 units. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) Runway quoted in est-hours overstates real supply; the binding constraint is the dispatcher fire rate (check_research_queue_throughput 2026-11-18: fired_24h 100, runnable 81, results_landed_24h 115, i.e. ~4 fires/h, 81 runnable ~ 19 h), so supply must be quoted in UNITS and fires/day, with est hours only as a diagnostic. (2) compute_router.class_backends promotes a cpu_light unit to kaggle_cpu when routing.est_minutes > research_compute.yaml kaggle_first.min_est_minutes (30), and cost-weights the value score by est hours; both inherit the inflated est, so which units go to Kaggle is decided by an authoring-time guess, not by measured cost. FIX: calibrate est from measured wall time per harness (a measured-runtime table keyed by run.command script + cells x arms, fed by the landed run manifests / workflow run durations), have the authoring contract (research/queue/PLANNING.md section 1b) read it, and give kaggle_first a threshold that is not est-based (for example a per-harness measured median, or an explicit routing.kaggle_preferred), so that correcting est does not silently move every unit back onto the runner. Manager decision 2026-11-18: est is KEPT on the units for now so the Kaggle routing stands; a measured-runtime note is added to routing.basis instead.
